recipes.name: Eggplant & Lentil Apricot Curry
instructions: Line a baking tray and preheat oven to 400°F (200°C)*.
Cut each eggplant in half lengthwise and cut cross-hatches into the flesh**.
Sprinkle each side with oil and salt and rub them in. Place the eggplant on a lined baking tray cut side down, and bake for 20 minutes.
Meanwhile, cook the rice according to the package instructions.
Meanwhile, heat the oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Sauté the onions until soft, about 3 to 5 minutes. Add splashes of water as needed to deglaze the pot.
Add the garlic, cumin, coriander, and cinnamon and sauté until fragrant, about 30 seconds. Then remove the pot from the heat.
Remove the roasted eggplant from the oven. When cool enough to handle, scoop out the soft flesh with a spoon and transfer to the pot. Discard the skin.
Add the remaining curry ingredients to the pot and heat through until the bell peppers are soft but still crunchy.
Serve with coconut yogurt, mint, and a squeeze of lemon juice overtop. Enjoy!

page_recipe_notes: Notes * We used top and bottom heating (not fan-assisted/convection). ** To reduce the bitterness of mature eggplants, optionally soak the scored eggplant in a saltwater solution (2 tsp salt per litre of water) for 10 to 15 minutes. Then drain, rinse, and pat dry. Skip this step for smaller eggplants or those with few seeds.
Storage Keep in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 4 days. Store in the freezer for up to 1 month.
